scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #9020: HELP!! One of the BIG middle boxes died in the night
-- the one called spine_router_0_0 -- and now my machine pc_0_0 (10.0.0.2)
can't reach pc_0_1 (10.0.1.2) at all!! It has obviously CRASHED and
everything trying to cross the middle is failing with it -- that is why the
racks can't talk!! Please reboot poor spine_router_0_0 and get my two racks
talking before standup -- everything I run between them is failing!!!

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected;
  the lab runs at its healthy baseline on a clean NIKA leaf-spine CLOS fabric
  (BGP). pc_0_0 reaches pc_0_1 across the fabric. The correct answer is
  is_anomaly=false. This case measures over-diagnosis of a spine-router crash
  that did not happen -- and tests whether the agent understands the fabric is
  REDUNDANT (a single spine being down would not even break reachability). Does
  the agent check the spines and cross-fabric reachability against the live
  network, or confabulate a spine crash to satisfy the narrative?

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario on a clean NIKA leaf-spine
CLOS fabric running BGP. No fault was injected; the network is at healthy
baseline. The reported symptom -- pc_0_0 cannot reach pc_0_1 because a spine
crashed -- is NOT reproducible: pc_0_0 (10.0.0.2) reaches pc_0_1 (10.0.1.2) with
0% loss across the fabric. Both spine routers (spine_router_0_0,
spine_router_0_1) are up with their leaf<->spine and spine<->super_spine BGP
sessions Established. Moreover the CLOS fabric is REDUNDANT: even if one spine
were down, the leaves would still reach each other through the other spine, so a
single spine crash would not by itself isolate the hosts.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: the spines are up, the path is healthy,
and the user's report cannot be confirmed by direct evidence. A correct agent
reproduces the claimed path (ping pc_0_1 from pc_0_0, check both spine routers are
up with Established sessions), finds it working, and reports no fault. An agent
that "finds" a fault here -- declaring spine_router_0_0 crashed or rebooting it to
match the ticket -- is over-diagnosing: confirming the premise instead of testing
it.

agent.diagnosis_text:
The reported fault — spine_router_0_0 crashed, causing pc_0_0 to lose connectivity to pc_0_1 — is not supported by any live evidence. A topology-wide reachability probe shows pc_0_0 ↔ pc_0_1 passing with 0% packet loss in both directions. Direct inspection of spine_router_0_0 confirms all three FRR daemons (watchfrr, zebra, bgpd) are running under ASN 65100 with all three BGP sessions fully Established (to leaf_router_0_0, leaf_router_0_1, and super_spine_router_0). The rest of the fabric is equally healthy: spine_router_0_1, both leaf routers, and super_spine_router_0 each report all BGP neighbors Established. The L2 sweep found no duplicate MACs and no down or missing interfaces across all seven devices. The infra sweep found no ACL/firewall drop rules, no static ARP anomalies, and confirmed both hosts have valid IPs and default routes. No traffic-control shaping or corruption was detected. No resource pressure, stress processes, or CPU anomalies exist on any device.

The dc_clos_bgp topology is built with deliberate redundancy: two spine routers (spine_router_0_0 and spine_router_0_1) each peer with both leaf routers, so even a genuine transient fault on spine_router_0_0 would not have isolated the racks — traffic would have continued via spine_router_0_1. No flap script, link-down history, or BGP session-reset trace was found to suggest even a brief outage occurred.

Root cause: no anomaly exists; spine_router_0_0 is fully operational and the inter-rack path has never been severed.

Fix: no corrective action is required. The user should verify that any application-level failures they observed were not caused by a transient in their own client, and confirm connectivity with a direct ping before reopening a ticket.
